## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of

consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.

# Audio Design Chapter — retro-arcade survival game GDD

## Problem statement

The GDD currently defines only SFX (§7.3 Audio Direction) and states background music is out of MVP scope with no musical direction defined. The game lacks a documented musical identity (scales, motifs, harmonic language, instrumentation, dynamic mixing, and state-driven music architecture) to guide composition and implementation when music is eventually built.

## Users

- **Audio designers and composers** — need a definitive musical language (scales/modes, motifs, progressions, instrumentation palette) to write consistent, on-brief music.
- **Technical audio programmers** — need the implementation contract (bus architecture, priority tiers, ducking, state machine, middleware guidance) to build or integrate the music system.
- **Game designers / producers** — need per-game-state emotional targets and transition rules to keep audio aligned with gameplay pacing.

User stories:

- As an audio designer, I want documented scales and motifs per game state, so my compositions match the game's emotional arc without guesswork.
- As a technical audio programmer, I want the music state machine and dynamic-mixing rules defined, so I can implement or configure the music engine against a fixed contract.
- As a producer, I want music explicitly scoped as design reference (out of MVP), so the shipped SFX scope (§7.3) is not disturbed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New chapter file created:** An **AI Hell Music System** chapter is saved as a Markdown GDD addendum at `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`. Its **musical substance** is taken from the producer's original *Music & Thematic Audio Design* brief (Phrygian Dominant + Lydian scales; Combat Motifs A and B and the ambient "Star Drift" motif; the combat, boss and ambient progressions; the FM 2–4 operator + chiptune implementation notes — reproduced under **Source material (A)** below) and laid out in the **8-section + 2-appendix** professional structure of the approved reference brief (Ross, v1.0, 16 October 2026): **1** Audio Vision Statement; **2** Musical Identity (2.1 Tonal Language, 2.2 Core Motifs, 2.3 Chord Progressions); **3** Instrumentation Palette; **4** Dynamic Mixing Rules; **5** State-Driven Music Transitions (5.1 Transition Design Principles, 5.2 Transition Matrix, 5.3 Stinger System); **6** Implementation Guidelines (6.1 Audio Middleware, 6.2 Music Event Architecture, 6.3 Parameter Mapping Table, 6.4 Technical Specifications, 6.5 Audio Budget Table); **7** Composer and Sound Designer Briefs (7.1 Composer Brief, 7.2 Sound Designer Brief); **8** Audio Accessibility; **Appendix A** Motif Reference Sheet; **Appendix B** Glossary. The reference brief is a **structure exemplar only** — its Tableau card-game substance (D Dorian, harpsichord/cello ensemble, card-table SFX, parlour ambience) must **not** be imported into AI Hell's chapter.
- [ ] **AC2 — GDD §7.3 references the chapter:** The "Background Music" subsection in GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction) is updated to link the new chapter file, while retaining the explicit statement that background music is **out of MVP scope** (design reference only; SFX remains the only in-scope audio).
- [ ] **AC3 — GDD §8 future-scope row updated:** The "Background music" row in §8 (Future Scope) references the new chapter file so the doc stays self-consistent.
- [ ] **AC4 — Doc-only change, no behaviour impact:** No game code, SFX behaviour, or runtime audio pipeline is changed; existing §7.3 SFX scope and the shipped ToneForge pipeline remain authoritative for the MVP.
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation:** A new docs guard `src/audioDesignChapterDocs.test.ts` (following the sibling `*Docs.test.ts` convention, e.g. `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`) asserts, and passes, that: (i) `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists; (ii) it carries all 8 numbered sections plus Appendix A and Appendix B of the approved reference structure; (iii) GDD §7.3's "Background Music" subsection links the chapter **and** still states music is out of MVP scope; (iv) the GDD §8 "Background music" row links the chapter. All links resolve, and any index/table-of-contents entries are updated.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (docs-only; confirms no accidental code impact).

## Constraints

- Music remains **"design reference, out of MVP scope"** — no change to the existing scope stance in GDD §7.3 or §8.
- The chapter is a **synthesis**, not a verbatim import (Q4/Q5, this session): the **musical content** is the producer's original retro-arcade brief reproduced faithfully (Source material (A)); the **document structure** follows the approved reference brief (author: Ross; version 1.0; dated 16 October 2026 — Source material (B)). The reference brief's Tableau card-game substance is **not** carried over.
- Follow the repo's docs naming/style conventions where sensible (singular Markdown addendum under `docs/`, referenced by relative link).
- UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- GDD §7.3 "Audio Direction" covers MVP SFX: baked ToneForge WAV pipeline, SFX event catalogue, per-enemy/per-player audio character, beat-synced explosion accents, and a one-paragraph "Background Music" subsection stating music is a nice-to-have, out of MVP.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" lists "Background music — Synthwave / retro electronic soundtrack" with no further detail.
- No existing work item implements or specifies background music; the work log contains no musical-identity design doc.

## Desired change

- Add the Audio Design Chapter (AI Hell musical content in the approved reference structure) as a standalone GDD addendum document.
- Point GDD §7.3's "Background Music" subsection and §8's future-scope row at the new document.
- Keep all gameplay/SFX/runtime behaviour untouched.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (new) — the Audio Design Chapter addendum (confirm filename at implementation)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 "Background Music" subsection updated with a link + scope note; §8 "Background music" row updated with a link
- `src/audioDesignChapterDocs.test.ts` (new) — docs guard following the sibling `*Docs.test.ts` convention
- `./README.md` (if it indexes docs) — optional link to the new chapter

## Related work

- **Update GDD audio design section and code comments (AH-0MTGS9DZ6001IFJR)** — completed; historical GDD §7.3 SFX additions, unrelated to music direction.
- **Update audio documentation (AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT)** — completed; ToneForge baked-asset pipeline docs; source of the current §7.3 scope language.
- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item.
- See also GDD §7.3 and §8, and `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` for the authoritative SFX cue catalogue.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-stance divergence (medium):** the chapter is "APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION" in tone while the GDD keeps music out of MVP. Mitigated by AC2/AC3 explicitly framing the chapter as design reference; implementation remains a future work item.
- **Middleware references (FMOD/Wwise) are forward-looking:** the game currently uses Phaser/Web Audio with baked assets (§7.3). The chapter's §9 middleware guidance is design intent for future integration, not an instruction to adopt FMOD/Wwise in the MVP. Noted in the chapter context if needed.
- **Content divergence from shipped SFX:** the chapter (§6.4) proposes procedural SFX recipes that differ from the shipped baked-ToneForge SFX catalogue. The chapter is an addendum; §7.3 remains authoritative for MVP SFX (per constraint). Recorded as an assumption.
- **Scope creep:** producer may later want chapter sections mapped into the live audio system — that is future implementation work, tracked separately, not part of this docs-only item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where in the GDD should the 'Music & Thematic Audio Design' content live? (a) replace the §7.3 'Background Music' paragraph with the full chapter; (b) keep the paragraph and add a new top-level section; (c) other." — Answer (user): "A — below is a full brief for the music. Use this to create a new file and refer to it from 7.3." Source: interactive reply. The final decision refines (a): rather than inlining, create a **new file** (`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`) and **refer to it from GDD §7.3**; adopted as AC1/AC2.
- Q2: "MVP scope statement for music — (a) keep music 'design reference, out of MVP scope'; (b) promote into MVP." — Answer (user): "A." Source: interactive reply. Adopted as the chapter's scope framing (AC2/AC3).
- Q3: "§8 Future Scope 'Background music' row — (a) update to reference the new chapter; (b) leave untouched." — Answer (user): "A." Source: interactive reply. Adopted as AC3.

### Plan-session clarifications (2026-10-23)

- Q4: "What should `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` actually contain? (a) author an AI Hell Music System chapter from the producer's *original retro-arcade* content (Phrygian Dominant + Lydian, Combat Motifs A/B & Star Drift, progressions, FM 2–4 op + chiptune notes) laid out in the approved reference brief's professional structure — the reference brief serving as format exemplar only; (b) import the reference brief verbatim as-is; (c) adapt the reference brief's content to AI Hell's palette; (d) freeform." — Answer (producer): "**1. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Research: the reference brief describes **Tableau**, a candlelit card game (D Dorian, harpsichord, cello, FMOD, card-table SFX) and is therefore not AI Hell's musical content — AI Hell is a retro-arcade bullet-hell (GDD §1: inspirations Galaxians/classic arcade shoot-'em-ups). The intake session on 2026-10-16 flagged this same conflict and the question was never answered, which left AC1 unverifiable until now. Adopted as the corrected **AC1**.
- Q5: "AC1 enumerates ten sections including *Recommended Scales & Modes* and *Playtesting & Iteration*, but the approved reference brief actually has eight numbered sections plus two appendices and contains no *Playtesting & Iteration* section. (a) correct AC1 to the brief's real structure; (b) keep the ten-section enumeration and build the chapter to it." — Answer (producer): "**2. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Evidence: reference brief table of contents (Source material (B)). Adopted as the corrected **AC1**.
- Q6: "The full source brief is not embedded in the work item (only section names are), so an implementer cannot reproduce content faithfully and AC1's verbatim requirement is unverifiable. (a) recover the full text from the 2026-10-16 intake session log and embed it in the work item; (b) producer re-supplies the brief." — Answer (producer): "**3. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Evidence: recovered from session log `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell--/2026-10-16T11-00-00-344Z_herdr-1792148399-1716826-22311.jsonl`. Adopted as **Source material (A)** below plus the reference-brief record held in this item's comments.
- Q7: Producer additionally instructed: "Also create a follow up work item to implement the design." — Answer (producer): directive recorded verbatim. Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Adopted as follow-up implementation work item **Build the music system from the Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** tracked separately (dependency: the implementation is blocked by this docs item), consistent with the *Scope creep* risk entry and the out-of-MVP scope stance (AC2/AC3).

### Source material (A) — producer's original *Music & Thematic Audio Design* brief (verbatim)

This is the authoritative **musical content** for the new chapter. Reproduced verbatim from the producer's original prompt (2026-10-16). UK-English and retro-arcade framing must be preserved; formatting artefacts in the original (runs such as `♭7Example (E)`) may be repaired into readable Markdown without changing substance.

```markdown
Music & Thematic Audio Design

This section defines the musical identity of the game, focusing on scales, motifs, harmonic language, and usage guidelines across gameplay states. The goal is to merge retro‑arcade space tension (Asteroids) with relentless survival energy (Vampire Survivors), using a coherent musical palette that supports procedural layering and dynamic intensity shifts.

🎼 1. Core Musical Identity

The soundtrack is built around two complementary scales:

Primary Combat Scale — Phrygian Dominant

Used for: wave combat, boss spawns, high‑intensity survival phases.

Scale Formula: 1 ♭2 3 4 5 ♭6 ♭7Example (E): E – F – G♯ – A – B – C – D

Why:

Retro‑arcade tension

Exotic, driving, instantly “space danger”

Works extremely well with FM bass, square leads, and arpeggiators

Provides strong melodic hooks with minimal notes

Secondary Ambient Scale — Lydian

Used for: menus, starfield travel, upgrade screens, low‑intensity exploration.

Scale Formula: 1 2 3 ♯4 5 6 7Example (C): C – D – E – F♯ – G – A – B

Why:

Bright, floating, cosmic

Contrasts the combat scale without breaking aesthetic cohesion

Ideal for pads, shimmering arps, and soft synth textures

🎵 2. Melodic Motifs

Motifs are intentionally short (2–6 notes) to support looping, procedural recombination, and chiptune‑style repetition.

Combat Motif A — “Incoming Wave”

Scale: Phrygian Dominant (E)Contour: Rising tension → abrupt dropNotes: E – F – G♯ – F – E – DUsage:

Triggered at the start of each enemy wave

Can be fragmented into E–F–G♯ for micro‑stingers

Works well as a 3‑note arpeggiated alert

Combat Motif B — “Survival Pulse”

Scale: Phrygian Dominant (E)Rhythmic Cell: Dotted + straightNotes: G♯ – A – G♯ – F – EUsage:

Mid‑combat loop

Easily reharmonized for intensity scaling

Can be doubled with FM bass for crunchy retro drive

Ambient Motif — “Star Drift”

Scale: Lydian (C)Contour: Floating, circularNotes: C – E – F♯ – E – D – CUsage:

Menu screens

Upgrade/shop interface

Slow arpeggiated background texture

🎹 3. Harmonic Progressions

Retro arcade music often avoids complex harmony, but these progressions provide structure while staying loop‑friendly.

Combat Progression (Phrygian Dominant)

E – F – E – D

Minimalist, modal, tense

Works with pulsing bass and rapid arps

Can be expanded to E – F – G♯ – F – E – D – C – D for boss phases

Boss Progression (Phrygian Dominant, extended)

E – C – D – F – E

Chromatic tension

Strong “danger escalation” feel

Supports heavy FM brass or distorted square leads

Ambient Progression (Lydian)

C – D – E – F♯

Bright, drifting, spacey

Works well with pads and slow-moving textures

Can be looped seamlessly or expanded to C – G – D – F♯

🔧 4. Implementation Notes

Motifs should be stored as atomic musical objects (interval sets + rhythm cells) for procedural recombination.

Combat layers should increase harmonic density (more voices, faster arps) rather than changing the motif.

Ambient layers should use long‑release envelopes and minimal rhythmic content.

FM synthesis (2–4 operators) and chiptune waveforms (square, triangle, noise) define the retro palette.

All motifs should be designed to loop cleanly at 1–2 bars for dynamic layering.
```

### Source material (B) — approved reference brief (structure exemplar)

The full 58 KB reference document (Ross, v1.0, 16 October 2026) that defines the **chapter structure** is recorded verbatim in a comment on this work item titled *Source material (B) — approved reference brief (structure exemplar), verbatim*. It describes the card game **Tableau**; treat its **section architecture, table layouts, parameter/stinger/matrix formats and glossary style** as the template, and its **musical and SFX substance as out of scope**.

## Verification approach

Docs-only change, but the repo convention is that cross-cutting docs slices ship with a `*Docs.test.ts` guard
(12 sibling guards exist, e.g. `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`, `src/enemyRosterDocs.test.ts`). The guard
for this item asserts file existence, the reference-brief section structure, and both GDD cross-links —
including the "out of MVP scope" sentence, so a future edit cannot silently promote music into the MVP.

Manual checks that complement the guard:
- Open `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` and confirm every Source material (A) element maps into the document
  (two scales, three motifs, three progressions, four implementation notes) — nothing dropped, nothing invented.
- Confirm no Tableau substance leaked in (no D Dorian as the home mode, no harpsichord/cello ensemble, no
  card-table SFX).
- Confirm §7.3's SFX catalogue, autoplay and rate-limiting text is untouched (AC4).

AC6 is satisfied by the standard dev-push gate (full suite); the guard above gives the changed-scope signal.

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

# Not all power-ups are appearing in the hull-full (hold-full) screen

> **Headline:** Restore full catalogue coverage in the hold-full choice overlay — every power-up and weapon drop (except the `reset` utility) must have a chance of appearing.

## Problem statement

The hold-full choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`) draws its options from the static
`CHOICE_POOL` list in `src/powerups/choice.ts`, which has not kept pace with the
catalogue. Ten shipped drops never appear: the five net-new power-ups (`frenzy`,
`chrono`, `thorns`, `salvage`, `strike`) and the five net-new weapons (`rear_guard`,
`broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`). An exhaustive test pins the
stale 21-entry list, so the gap is invisible to the suite. All ten should have a
chance of appearing when the hold fills.

## Users

- **Player** — fills the mineral hold, opens the hold-full choice, and expects any
  power-up/weapon he has ever seen in the field (or the catalogue) to be a candidate.
  - *As a player, I want Frenzy, Chrono Field, Thorn Field, Salvage and Orbital
    Strike to be offered when my hold fills, so I can build toward the power-up
    I am collecting, rather than only ever being able to earn them as field drops.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Pool covers the full catalogue, with no gating.** `CHOICE_POOL` contains every
  power-up id (`frenzy`, `chrono`, `thorns`, `salvage`, `strike` added) and every weapon id
  (`rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug` added), minus `reset`
  only, with no unlock-state filter and no per-scene copies. A regression test asserts the
  pool equals the full catalogue minus `reset`, replacing the stale exhaustive assertion in
  `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`.
- **AC2 — New options are fully functional when picked.** Each of the ten added ids,
  selected as a base grant in the hold-full choice, applies through the existing shared
  reward path (`applyMineralChoiceReward` + `effectsRegistry.applyCollect`), renders a
  name/description from the shared catalogues (`getHelpDescription`/`WEAPON_NAMES`/
  `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`), carries the ★ New badge when unowned, and behaves identically
  whether granted in the game (`PlayScene`) or a gym (`GymFormationScene`,
  `GymWeaponLeveling`).
- **AC3 — Ownership/level-up offers continue to work for the new ids.** `buildChoiceCandidates`
  suppresses the base entry for an owned new item and emits its `weapon-level`/`power-up-level`
  offer with a correct `changeSummary`, for each of the ten new ids (the five weapons are
  already in `LEVELABLE_WEAPON_IDS`; the five power-ups already have level curves).
- **AC4 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,** including code
  comments (`src/powerups/choice.ts` module prose), the GDD §4.5 pool description
  ("all power-ups plus Spread/Dual/Rapid/Nova/Mortar/Arc") and any affected test docs.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** The Power Pellet
  removal guard (`powerPelletRemoval.test.ts`) and the choice-strategy suite remain green,
  with the "does not over-remove" guard extended to all sixteen power-ups.

## Constraints

- **Keep the pool single-source.** The game and every gym must consume the same
  `CHOICE_POOL`/`randomChoiceStrategy`; no divergent per-scene copies (gym↔game parity,
  AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **No weighting change.** Base-entry weights stay uniform at 1.0× with the existing
  1.35× owned-upgrade bonus (Q3-A); this item fixes eligibility only. Field-drop rarity
  tuning is out of scope.
- **No unlock-state gating** (Q2-N/A): the mini-boss locked pool is being retired.
- **`reset` stays excluded** — it removes weapons rather than granting one (documented).
- **Do not touch the `unlocks.ts` machinery**; removal of the locked pool is owned by
  AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD. This item only widens the choice pool.

## Existing state

- `CHOICE_POOL` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) — 21 entries: 11 power-ups + 10 weapons.
- Stale exhaustive assertion in `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` pins exactly
  those 21 ids.
- The ten missing ids already exist everywhere else: `types.ts` catalogue, `rules.ts`
  weight tables (`POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS`/`WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, `defaultPowerUpWeights`/
  `defaultWeaponWeights`), `effects.ts` registry, `powerUpLevels.ts` curves, `icons.ts`,
  HUD, gym help — only the hold-full pool omits them.
- `LEVELABLE_WEAPON_IDS` already includes the five new weapons; `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`
  already includes the five new power-ups — so level-up/ownership paths need no new code.

## Desired change

Add the ten missing ids to `CHOICE_POOL`; the pool becomes every power-up and weapon
drop id except `reset` (16 + 15 = 31 entries). Update/extend the regression tests so the
pool can never silently drift from the catalogue again, and refresh the stale docs
(choice module prose + GDD §4.5). No change to the selection strategy, weighting,
reward application, or unlock machinery.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add the ten ids to `CHOICE_POOL`; refresh module doc:
  "the base drop pool (Shield–Mineral Scoop plus the collectable weapon drops …)".
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — replace the exhaustive 21-entry assertion
  with a catalogue-derived invariant (pool ⊇ all power-up ids ∪ all weapon ids minus `reset`).
- `src/powerups/powerPelletRemoval.test.ts` — extend `REMAINING_POWER_UP_IDS` to the full
  sixteen so the "does not over-remove" guard covers the net-new power-ups.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` / `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **no change** (locked-pool
  removal is a separate item); verify only.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 hold-full pool wording ("all power-ups plus
  Spread/Dual/Rapid/Nova/Mortar/Arc" → full catalogue minus `reset`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` —
  consume the widened default pool automatically; verify gym tests that assert offered sets.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "hull-full screen" == the hold-full choice overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`), opened when the mineral hold fills (GDD §4.5); "hull" is a
  mistyping of "hold". Confirmed by the operator's answers referencing hold-full behaviour.
- **Assumption (AC1):** the locked-pool retirement (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) will land;
  until it does, a hold-full grant of a formerly-locked weapon is acceptable (they already
  drop in the field via the weight tables).
- **Risk — widening dilutes the pool:** holding the option count at 3 while the pool grows
  from 21 → 31 makes each specific pick slightly rarer. Accepted by Q3-A (uniform
  weighting kept); rebalance is a candidate follow-up item if playtests complain.
- **Risk — gym test drift:** gym launchers inherit the widened pool automatically; tests
  asserting exact option sets may need updates — accounted for in AC2.
- **Scope creep guard:** rarity tuning for field weights, the mini-boss reward UI
  (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) and `unlocks.ts` changes are *not* part of this item.

## Related work

- AH-0MVI4KTD8000FBJ7 — this work item.
- AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD — "Mini-Boss rewards become valuable": removes the locked-pool
  reward system; makes this item's no-gating decision stable (`related-to`).
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — "Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool": origin of
  the locked weapons now entering the pool.
- AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1 / AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z — epic introducing the five net-new power-ups
  (frenzy/chrono/thorns/salvage/strike).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (single shared implementation).
- AH-0MUY47W62005FF74 / AH-0MVCFB00Y004AQ2Z — owned-upgrade 1.35× weighting (unchanged).
- AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08 — Power Pellet removal guard (must stay green).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which missing drops should enter the hold-full pool — (A) only the 5 net-new
  power-ups, or (B) the power-ups **and** the 5 mini-boss-locked weapons?"
  — Answer (operator): **B** — both categories; pool = every drop id except `reset`.
  Source: interactive reply in intake session.
  Research: `CHOICE_POOL` holds 21 ids vs 16 + 16 in the catalogue; the only missing
  weapons are the five locked ones (`reset` is a documented exclusion).
- Q2: "Should the five mini-boss-locked weapons respect the mini-boss unlock state in the

  — Answer (operator): **N/A** — "We are changing the mini-boss rewards system in another

  ("Mini-Boss rewards become valuable", open, stage `idea`) describes a wheel-based

- Q3: "Weighting within the hold-full pool — (A) keep uniform base-entry weight, or
  (B) mirror field-drop rarity?"
  — Answer (operator): **A** — keep uniform; fix eligibility only. Source: interactive
  reply. Rationale: report is about absence, not rarity.

## How to verify

```bash
# Changed-scope gate (unit + smoke) via the project test skill:
/skill:test

# Targeted inspection while implementing:
rg -n "CHOICE_POOL" src/powerups/choice.ts
```

# Predict enemy movement (bot) — Intake Brief

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

The demo/attract bot already **predicts incoming fire** (in-flight bullets and
fire-tell shots) and **leads moving targets** when aiming, but its
**collision avoidance treats every hazard — enemy, asteroid, boss — as a
stationary point**. The steering filter (`evaluateDirection` in
`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) only rejects a bearing that drives
*toward a hazard's current position* inside `dangerMargin`, and the code
itself notes *"The snapshot exposes no hazard velocity, so this is
positional."* A fast crossing enemy is therefore not where the bot expected
when the ship arrives, and the demo ship can be seen ramming enemies it could
have avoided — enemies are positional hazards by design ("enemies are the
bullets", GDD §2.4, and AH-0MT7USMWN0071UF5). We want the bot to avoid where a
**moving** hazard will be, not just where it is now.

## Users

- **Viewer of the attract/demo mode** (primary): expects a believable pilot
  that does not collide with enemies when a safe path exists.
- **Designer using the bot-tuning gym / balance harness** (secondary): wants
  the prediction horizon exposed as a live knob and a reproducible,
  test-based guarantee that the bot avoids predicted collisions.

### Example user stories

- As a **viewer of the demo**, I want the bot to veer off the path of a fast
  crossing enemy before we collide, so the demo looks competent.
- As a **designer**, I want a `hazardPredictionHorizon` slider in the bot gym,
  so I can tune how far ahead the bot looks without editing code.
- As a **developer**, I want the prediction to be pullable from a deterministic
  60 Hz test, so the fix is verified rather than eyeballed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Bot-side hazard-velocity estimation.** The bot derives a velocity
   for every live hazard (enemy, asteroid, boss) **itself**, by tracking
   per-hazard position deltas across decision ticks in `BotMemory` (keyed by a
   stable enemy id exposed through the snapshot seam — no per-archetype entity
   velocity code). The estimate is deterministic for identical
   snapshot+`dt` sequences, resets with the brain, and is clamped so spurious
   jumps (wrap-around, respawn) cannot produce an absurd velocity. A hazard
   with no movement history or no velocity estimate is treated as stationary —
   exactly today's behaviour.
- **AC2 — Predictive hazard collision avoidance in steering.** When
   `hazardPredictionEnabled` is on, `evaluateDirection` evaluates each
   candidate bearing against **moving** hazards using a closest-approach solve
   over `hazardPredictionHorizon` (the same relative-motion primitive already
   used for bullets): a bearing is *unsafe* when the ship (moving at the
   candidate-bearing speed) and the hazard (moving at its estimated velocity)
   are predicted to come within `threatRadius`; otherwise today's positional
   `dangerMargin` rule still applies. The kiting threat gate in the `engage`
   behaviour (imminent collision) uses the same predicted-collision test
   instead of proximity alone. Disabled or zero-velocity cases reproduce the
   current positional behaviour bit-for-bit.
- **AC3 — Designer-tunable in the bot tuning gym.** New knobs
   `hazardPredictionEnabled` (toggle) and `hazardPredictionHorizon` (seconds,
   look-ahead window, recommended default `0.6`) are added to
   `COMPETENT_BOT_TUNABLES`, registered in `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` as
   documented sliders/toggles with bounds, and applied live by `GymBotTuning`
   exactly like the existing aim-lead knobs (AC4 pattern of
   AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98).
- **AC4 — Deterministic validation.** Unit tests cover: (a) the estimator
   producing a stable velocity from position deltas and zero for a stationary
   hazard; (b) `evaluateDirection` rejecting a bearing predicted to cross a
   moving hazard within the horizon and accepting the same bearing when the
   hazard is stationary or the feature is off. A deterministic 60 Hz
   integration test (shared `botSteering.integration.test.ts` style) asserts
   that a straight crossing enemy which **collides** with prediction off is
   **evaded** with prediction on — the recorded minimum ship–hazard distance
   stays ≥ `threatRadius` (minus tolerance) — while disabled-mode output stays
   equal to today's.
- **AC5 — Documentation updated.** `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` (competent-bot
   sections), the attract/demo section of `docs/Game Design Document.md`, and
   the module docs of every touched bot file describe the bot-side velocity
   estimation and the predictive hazard-collision avoidance. All related
   documentation is updated (code comments, README, relevant docs entries).
- **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes
   (including typecheck and build).

## Constraints

- **Shared code, gym↔game parity.** All new behaviour lives in the shared
  `src/ai/` modules (`BotMemory`, `worldModel`, `competent/steering.ts`) and is
  consumed identically by `PlayScene` and the bot gym — no divergent copies;
  the duplicate-body guard in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stays green.
- **Deterministic and wall-clock free.** The estimator advances only on the
  injected snapshot sequence and `dt`; no `Math.random()` or `Date.now()` in
  the decision path. It is reset with the brain (`resetBotMemory`) so runs
  replay bit-for-bit on the same seed/inputs.
- **Snapshot seam is the source of truth.** Estimation happens bot-side; the
  existing entity-exposed `vx`/`vy` (Asteroid, LaneTraffic) continues to feed
  the aim-lead consumer only. Choice of velocity source is **bot-side
  estimation (operator Q2 = B)**, not entity-exposed.
- **No regression to reverse-thrust restraint** (AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2): reverse
  remains reserved for trouble/correction; this change only adds predicted
  collisions to the existing threat set.
- **Backwards compatibility.** With prediction disabled (or a hazard whose
  velocity estimate is zero/absent) the steering output is exactly today's;
  existing tests that pin positional hazard behaviour remain green (unless
  the default-on setting is shown by the AC4 test to change a specific
  pinned expectation, in which case that test is updated deliberately).

## Existing state

- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `predictIncomingFire` + `classifyShot`
  already predict **bullets** by closest approach over a horizon;
  `BotWorld.hazards` is `BotWorldPoint[]` (position only).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection` rejects
  unsafe bearings: walls, **positional** hazards, and **predicted** shots.
  `closestApproach(px,py,pvx,pvy,qx,qy,qvx,qvy,horizon)` already exists and is
  reusable for hazards.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — `engage` kiting fires on "an
  imminent hazard collision" but that test is `distance < dangerMargin`
  (positional).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — survival *urgency* is keyed only to
  threatening shots; positional hazard proximity is not part of the urgency.
  (Whether to extend urgency is a scope note, see Risks.)
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — `BotEnemy` carries optional `vx`/`vy` only when
  the source entity exposes a physics body (Asteroid, LaneTraffic); there is
  **no stable enemy id** today.
- `src/ai/framework/memory.ts` — `BotMemory` holds commitment, ticks and goal
  scratch; a velocity tracker slot fits the same deterministic-memory pattern.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` + `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` +
  `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — the slider/registry/store pattern the new
  knobs follow (from AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98 AC4).
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9 (competent bot), `docs/Game Design Document.md`
  §"Attract / demo mode" — canonical descriptions to update.

## Desired change

1. Add a deterministic, bot-side **hazard-velocity tracker** to `BotMemory`:
   on each `decide(snapshot, dt)` it records each live hazard's position and
   estimates velocity from the previous tick's position divided by `dt`,
   clamped to a sane maximum; hazards missing from one tick keep their last
   estimate (decay optional) until re-seen.
2. Expose a **stable per-enemy id** through the snapshot seam (a bot-side
   identity assigned by the snapshot builder — no per-archetype entity edits)
   so the tracker can correlate enemies across ticks.
3. Carry estimated velocity onto `BotWorld.hazards` (an extended hazard point
   with optional `vx`/`vy`), keeping `buildBotWorld` pure and backward
   compatible when no velocities are supplied.
4. In `evaluateDirection`, when `hazardPredictionEnabled` is on and a hazard
   has a non-zero estimate, run the same `closestApproach` prediction used for
   bullets: reject the candidate if predicted separation within
   `hazardPredictionHorizon` is under `threatRadius`; keep the positional
   `dangerMargin` rule otherwise.
5. Extend the `engage` kiting threat gate to use the same predicted-collision
   test. Update the survival-urgency documentation only if the AC4
   integration test shows the survive goal must react earlier to an imminent
   predicted collision (see Risks — kept out of core scope).
6. Add `hazardPredictionEnabled` and `hazardPredictionHorizon` tunables,
   register them in the gym, and document per AC3/AC5.
7. Add the estimator, steering and integration tests per AC4.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — stable enemy id on `BotEnemy`/`BotEnemySource` and
  the builder (`WeakMap`-assigned counter, bot-side only).
- `src/ai/framework/memory.ts` — hazard-velocity tracker slot in `BotMemory`
  (+ `resetBotMemory` reset).
- New `src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts` (or in `worldModel.ts`) — pure
  per-hazard velocity estimation from position deltas + `dt`.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — hazards carry optional `vx`/`vy`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection` predictive
  hazard rejection; anticipated `closestApproach` reuse.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — kiting imminent-collision test.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — `hazardPredictionEnabled` /
  `hazardPredictionHorizon`.
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — new sliders.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`, new estimator test, and any test
  pinning `BotMemory` shape.
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, README if the
  feature surfaces there, module headers of touched files.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98 — Bot rotation skills** (completed): the aim-lead and
  `skill` half of "predict enemy movement"; this item closes the *avoidance*
  half (operator Q1 = A) and reuses its tunables/gym/test patterns.
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ — Smart capture bot** (completed): origin of the
  survival-first bot and its bullet-path prediction; hazards stayed
  positional there.
- **AH-0MUX43QS4005SFJ3 — Bot decision logic: survival-first heuristic**
  (completed): the legacy decision layer this change deliberately does **not**
  extend (legacy parity best-effort, like aim-lead).
- **AH-0MT7USMWN0071UF5 — Clarify enemy pass-through and bullet-blocking
  rules in GDD** (completed): enemies are positional hazards — no
  enemy–enemy collision, but the ship collides with them, which is exactly
  the hazard the bot must predict around.
- **AH-0MU8QW2XS001HE2A / AH-0MU44M90T003EQ2G** — surfaced by the automated
  related-work scan (report auto-inserted into the item description); noise
  (audio seam / placement strategy), not blockers.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (velocity source, operator Q2 = B):** hazard velocity is
  **estimated bot-side from position deltas**; no per-archetype entity
  velocity work is done. Entity-exposed velocity keeps feeding the aim-lead
  consumer only. Estimator clamp bounds the error from a wrap/respawn jump.
- **Assumption (defaults):** `hazardPredictionEnabled` defaults **on** with a
  modest horizon (0.6 s is the proposed default) because the additional
  rejection can only make the bot safer; if this breaks a test that pins
  positional behaviour, that test's expectation is deliberately updated (the
  AC4 integration test is the arbiter).
- **Risk (medium):** stable identity for enemies is not in the snapshot

## Goal

As a player/operator, changing the Control Scheme in Settings must actually persist. Today it silently fails once the browser's localStorage quota is full, because the dev telemetry sink fills that quota. The fix removes telemetry from localStorage entirely: the dev JSONL sink becomes an **in-memory, per-run buffer** that is uploaded straight from memory and reset at the start of each run.

## Operator report (verbatim)

> AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU is still not working. It seems the setting is not being saved. 1) selecting settings and change to 4 directional 2) back to menu 3) open settings and the control profile is back to asteroids

Environment (operator-confirmed): `npm run dev -- --host`, playing at http://100.106.5.111:5173/. The row visibly shows Four Directional after the change, then reverts to Asteroids after re-opening Settings.

Related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU (mid-run scheme honouring, commit 3c75eb4c) and AH-0MVI7LRCJ006Q8SA (the control-scheme setting feature).

## Root cause (confirmed from the operator's console)

```
Uncaught QuotaExceededError: Failed to execute 'setItem' on 'Storage':
Setting the value of 'ai_hell_settings' exceeded the quota.
    at saveSettings (settingsStore.ts:262)
    at SettingsScene._persist (SettingsScene.ts:745)
    at SettingsScene.setControlScheme ...
```

Measured on current `dev` (headless Chromium, normal play): ~50.8 telemetry ticks/s at ~1,267 B/tick = **~64 KB/s** written to `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`. The ~5 MiB per-origin quota is exhausted after **~1.4 minutes of play**. From that moment every `localStorage.setItem` throws — including `saveSettings` — so the Control Scheme (and any other setting) silently fails to persist and reverts to the last saved value.

Three defects share this cause:

1. **Settings become unsaveable** once the quota fills (the reported symptom).
2. **Silent telemetry truncation**: `recorder.deliver` counts sink-write failures (`failedBatches`) without throwing, so a long run is quietly head-truncated; any single run longer than ~65 s cannot fit in localStorage at all.
3. **Cross-run duplication in uploaded recordings**: nothing clears the sink between runs, and the run-end upload POSTs the **whole accumulated sink**. Run 2's `recordings/session-*.jsonl` therefore contains runs 1+2, run 3's all three — the recordings double-count and the automatic evaluation sees stale records.

## Approach (operator-approved rescope — supersedes the earlier "cap the sink" plan)

Telemetry must not use localStorage at all. Design:

1. **Dev JSONL sink becomes in-memory and per-run.** `createTelemetrySink`'s `jsonl` case creates a run-scoped in-memory writer (the existing `createMemoryLineWriter()` in `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` already provides the primitive) instead of `createLocalStorageLineWriter(...)`. The buffer is **reset on `startRun`**, so each run starts clean — this is the operator's "clear it at the start of the next game" and it removes both the cross-run duplication and any need for a cap/eviction policy.
2. **Upload from memory.** `uploadDevTelemetry` reads the in-memory buffer content via an injected `readSink` seam (already the shape of `DevTelemetryUploadOptions.readSink`) wired to the recorder's buffer, instead of `localStorage.getItem(...)`. Endpoint, content type, NDJSON body and the run-end fire-and-forget behaviour are unchanged, so `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` and the evaluation pipeline need no change.
3. **Expose the buffer to the dev CLI tooling.** The three Node scripts currently read the run via `page.evaluate(localStorage.getItem('ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl'))`. Add a dev-gated page accessor following the existing `window.__aiHellScenario` / `window.__aiHellRunState` convention — e.g. `window.__aiHellTelemetry = { read(): string }` installed by the dev-gated wiring, never written in a production bundle (same static-elimination pattern as `loadDevTelemetryUploader`). Update:
   - `scripts/record-session.mjs` (read the run out of the page),
   - `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (pre-clip reset + post-clip read; the pre-boot `removeItem` becomes a buffer reset/no-op),
   - `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` (assert against the page buffer instead of the localStorage key).
   `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` is file/stdin based — unaffected.
4. **Harden `saveSettings` as a cheap safety net.** Wrap the `setItem` in `src/core/settingsStore.ts` so a full or unavailable storage can never throw out of a Phaser input handler; on failure log one clear `console.warn`. This is defence in depth: with telemetry off localStorage, the settings record is the only writer left.
5. **Update the pinned contract + docs.** `src/telemetry/devUpload.test.ts` pins "sink content left intact after a successful upload"; replace that with the stronger "the dev sink never touches localStorage" (plus "a run start resets the buffer"). Update `docs/TELEMETRY.md` and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, which document the localStorage key.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — memory sink as the `jsonl` default; keep/rescope `createLocalStorageLineWriter` (it becomes unused by the runtime path; per the coding disciplines, report rather than silently delete — decide explicitly whether to keep it as exported test-covered API or remove it).
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` / `src/telemetry/index.ts` — buffer access + reset-on-`startRun` seam.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` — read from memory (default `readSink`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (or the `runTelemetry` wire-up) — install the dev-gated `window.__aiHellTelemetry` accessor.
- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — quota-defensive `saveSettings`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`.
- Tests: `src/telemetry/sinks.test.ts`, `devUpload.test.ts`, `recorder.test.ts`, `settingsStore` tests, plus the script tests.
- Docs: `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The dev telemetry path never reads or writes localStorage — no `setItem`/`getItem` on `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` from the runtime path (unit test asserts the resolved `jsonl` sink is the in-memory writer and that recording + upload complete with `localStorage` unavailable).
- AC2: Each run's uploaded body contains **only that run's** records: `startRun` resets the buffer (unit test: two sequential runs, second upload has exactly one `run_header` and no records from the first run).
- AC3: With localStorage pre-filled to overflow, changing the Control Scheme in Settings persists and reopening Settings shows the new value, with no `QuotaExceededError` in the console (browser-level check, menu and pause origins).
- AC4: A single run of arbitrary length is captured in full (no quota-based truncation); the buffer is released on run end after upload.
- AC5: `npm run record`, `npm run capture` (action-intensity series export) and `npm run verify-dev-telemetry` still work end-to-end against the new page accessor; `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` behaviour unchanged.
- AC6: `saveSettings` never throws out of an input handler; a residual storage failure logs exactly one clear `console.warn`.
- AC7: Docs (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`) describe the in-memory per-run buffer and no longer claim a localStorage key; the dev gating of the page accessor is documented and enforced (no accessor in a production bundle).
- AC8: Full project test suite passes (`/skill:test --type full` at the dev-push gate).

## Out of scope / follow-up

- **Incremental (per-batch) upload for crash resilience**: with in-memory buffering, a page reload/crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail (today it survives a reload but silently stops at the quota). Streaming batches to the dev server would recover at most one batch (~1.3 s) of loss; raised as a separate discovered-from item rather than folded in here.
- **Cutting the production/player tick rate to ~4 Hz (0.25 s)**: separate decision (prefer a time-based `TICK_INTERVAL_MS` over the current per-tick probability `VITE_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE`); not required by this fix, since production telemetry is consent-gated and uses the remote sink (no localStorage).

# Salvage has no visible effect (AH-0MVJ72I8O0009T09)

## Problem statement

While the **Salvage** bounty window is active, each destroyed non-hazard enemy
drops the level-resolved bonus minerals at the wreck, but those minerals render
as exactly the same gold dots as every ordinary mineral. The bounty therefore
has no *visible* effect: the player cannot tell whether the extra minerals came
from Salvage, and the pickup feels inert even though the mechanic is wired.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (bounty chooser):** *As a player who collected or chose Salvage, when
  I destroy an enemy I want the bonus minerals to look different from ordinary
  minerals, so I can see the bounty paying out and judge whether it was worth
  the pickup.*
- **Player (economy reading):** *As a player reading the mineral field, I want
  ordinary mineral drops to stay gold, so the baseline economy stays readable
  and the orange dots uniquely mean "Salvage bonus".*

## Current behaviour (verified in the repo)

- `EffectsRegistry.salvageBonusMinerals()` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) returns
  `0` unless the timed window is active, otherwise the level-resolved
  `salvageMinerals` (curve base **1** → cap **4**, k=0.35).
- The shared kill seam adds exactly that many extra minerals at the wreck
  through `scatterMineralDrops(...)`:
  - `PlayScene` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, in the kill handler, just after
    `resolveMineralKillDrops`);
  - `GymFormationScene._dropMineralsForKill`
    (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
  Both guard with `isNonBlockingHazard(...)` / the `getSizeTier` test, so
  **asteroids and lane hazards are excluded** — Salvage pays out for destroyed
  **ships** only, even though the original report assumed "ships and/or
  asteroids".
- The HUD already lists a Salvage row while the window is active
  (`src/ui/HUD.ts`, `case 'salvage'` → `reg.isActive(id)`), so a countdown
  readout exists. The visibility gap is purely the **drop rendering**.
- `Mineral` hard-codes `MINERAL_COLOR` (`0xffdd44`, gold) in `_drawBody()`
  (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`), and `scatterMineralDrops` accepts no colour, so
  every mineral in the game and in every gym is visually identical.

## Desired change

Give **Salvage bonus minerals their own colour — orange** — while every other
mineral stays gold, in the game and in every gym, through one shared code path.
The change is cosmetic: an orange salvage mineral is still worth exactly one
mineral.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Orange salvage drops.** While the Salvage window is active, the bonus
   minerals spawned at a destroyed enemy's wreck render **orange**, and every
   other mineral (asteroid drop, enemy re-drop, seeded gym field, drone spill)
   continues to render **gold**. Covered by unit tests in the game
   (`PlayScene`) and in the formation gym (`GymFormationScene`).
2. **Single source of colour.** The orange is defined once as a named constant
   (`MINERAL_SALVAGE_COLOR`) beside `MINERAL_COLOR` in `src/core/constants.ts`;
   `Mineral` accepts an optional colour (default `MINERAL_COLOR`), so all
   existing callers keep the gold default unchanged.
3. **One shared seam (gym↔game parity).** Game and gyms spawn salvage drops
   through **one** shared helper (e.g. `scatterSalvageMineralDrops` next to
   `scatterMineralDrops`), and the repo-wide defined-once guard in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` covers it, so the colour
   and scatter maths cannot drift between `PlayScene` and the gyms.
4. **No behaviour, economy or RNG change.** Each salvage mineral is still worth
   one mineral, the bonus count still comes from
   `salvageBonusMinerals()`, asteroids remain excluded, and the scatter helper
   consumes the same two RNG draws per drop in the same order (existing
   determinism/draw-order tests stay green).
5. **Visible in a real run.** With Salvage active, an enemy kill leaves orange
   dots on the field next to any gold drops, so the effect is legible to the
   player without reading the HUD.
6. **Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4 Salvage entry / §4.4.1 minerals
   "Dropping" bullet), `README.md`'s mineral section and the relevant code
   comments all describe the orange salvage drop.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Cosmetic only: no new drop type, no value change, no magnet/scoop behaviour
  change, no HUD redesign.
- Keep the existing `scatterMineralDrops` signature backwards compatible
  (optional colour parameter or an additive helper), so the many current
  callers (asteroid drops, enemy re-drops, collector-drone spill, gym seeding)
  are untouched.
- The orange must be clearly distinct from gold and from existing gameplay
  colours (enemy fire reds/pinks, power-up bubble colours); confirm the chosen
  value against the bullet/pickup palettes before picking it.
- No new procedural timers or per-frame work — this is a fill colour at spawn.

## Existing state

- Salvage is already fully wired (`AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z`): bonus minerals spawn
  through the shared kill seam in `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`, and the
  integration test `AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z — Salvage adds bonus minerals at a
  destroyed enemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) proves the count grows.
- The only missing piece is a distinguishable render colour for those drops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — add `MINERAL_SALVAGE_COLOR` (orange) with a doc
  comment next to `MINERAL_COLOR`.
- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — optional `color` on `MineralConfig`, `_drawBody()`
  uses `config.color ?? MINERAL_COLOR`, plus an optional colour argument (or
  additive helper) on the scatter function.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — shared re-export / seam for the
  salvage-coloured scatter helper so both scenes import one thing.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — use the shared salvage-drop helper.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — use the same shared salvage-drop
  helper (parity).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend the defined-once
  guard to the new helper.
- Tests: `src/entities/__tests__/Mineral.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (or
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`), a
  `GymFormationScene` salvage-colour test, and
  `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` if the seam lives there.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 Salvage entry and the §4.4.1
  minerals "Dropping" bullet) and `README.md` (minerals section).

## Related work

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z — Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed):** wired
  `salvageBonusMinerals()` into the shared kill seam (game + gyms). This item is
  the visual follow-up to that wiring.
- **AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1 — 5 net-new power-ups (completed):** introduced the
  Salvage catalogue entry, its level curves (1 → 4 bonus minerals, 10 → 20 s)
  and the HUD readout.
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold (completed):** owns the `Mineral` entity, `MINERAL_COLOR` and the
  shared scatter maths this change extends.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — Document gym-parity principle (completed):** the rule
  that an enabled behaviour runs the same code in the game and every gym; this
  brief therefore demands one shared salvage-drop helper.
- **AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S — Asteroids drop more lives (completed):** precedent for
  a kill-drop variant added to the same shared kill seam.
- Repo/docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (Salvage) and §4.4.1
  (Minerals, the Ship's Hold & the Power-Up Choice); `README.md` minerals
  section; `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` (shared kill-drop rule).

### Automated find-related report

- **AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4** – Power ups need to be larger (completed)
- **AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S** – Asteroids drop more lives (completed)
- **AH-0MU8FOQM0007D94Z** – Enemy Config + Factory Wiring + Unit Tests (completed)

Repository file matches: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Out of scope (follow-up candidates, not this item)

- Adding a HUD "Salvage +N" bonus suffix or a pickup flourish. If the colour
  alone proves insufficient, raise a `discovered-from:AH-0MVJ72I8O0009T09`
  item rather than widening this one.
- Making Salvage apply to asteroids/hazards (it deliberately does not).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a distinct colour is enough to make the bounty legible.
  Justification: the complaint is that the extra drops are indistinguishable;
  the HUD already exposes the active window and its bonus level.
- **Risk (visual collision):** orange may read like enemy fire or a hazard.
  Mitigation: pick a hue/saturation clearly outside the enemy-bullet palette,
  keep the small-dot silhouette, and note the choice in the constant's comment.
- **Risk (parity drift):** if `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each passed a
  colour literal they could diverge. Mitigation: one shared helper + the
  defined-once equivalence guard.
- **Risk (RNG determinism):** touching the scatter helper could reorder draws.
  Mitigation: additive/optional parameter only; existing draw-order tests must
  stay green.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "while I am here" ideas (new mineral tiers, value
  changes, HUD redesign) are recorded above as out of scope, not folded in.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **No clarifying questions were needed.** The seed context ("make the extra
  items dropped a different colour, perhaps orange") already fixes the desired
  outcome. Research resolved the remaining unknowns from the repo:
  - Salvage applies to destroyed **ships only**, not asteroids — the kill seams
    exclude non-blocking hazards (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`).
  - The extra drops are already spawned (`AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z`), so this is a
    rendering-only change.
  - The HUD already shows the active Salvage row, so no HUD work is required.
- **Assumptions recorded as resolved decisions:** orange = the salvage colour;
  everything else stays gold; the change is cosmetic (1 mineral per dot); the
  colour is exposed as a constant plus an optional `Mineral` config field.

## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: with the dev JSONL sink moving to an in-memory per-run buffer (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), a page reload or crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail. Streaming telemetry batches to the dev server during the run — instead of one run-end upload — bounds that loss to at most one flushed batch (~64 records, ~1.3 s of play) and removes the page-reload regression that localStorage previously masked.

## Context

- Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3 (in-memory dev sink; this item is explicitly deferred there).
- Current flow: the JsonlTelemetrySink buffers records in memory, flushes batches of 64 to the sink, and the whole run is POSTed once at run end (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash before that POST loses the entire run's telemetry; a reload also loses the buffer entirely once it is no longer localStorage-backed.
- Dev only: the same reasoning applies to the production remote sink, which already streams batches via `HttpTelemetryTransport` (with retry/backoff), so production is not affected.

## Proposed design

- Send each flushed batch to the dev endpoint as it is produced (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) instead of (or in addition to) the run-end upload.
- The server (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) currently stores each upload as one complete `session-<stamp>.jsonl` and runs the automatic evaluation per upload; a per-batch POST would create many tiny recordings and repeated evaluations. The endpoint (or a new `part` protocol) must therefore either:
  - append JSONL records to the run's open session file keyed by a run id/seed, and evaluate once at run end, or
  - keep the run-end upload and add a lightweight "heartbeat/checkpoint" mechanism that only recovers the tail on demand.
- UX/offline: batches sent while the dev server is unreachable should stay in the memory buffer (or a bounded queue) and be retried at run end; at most one batch may be lost on a hard crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A mid-run crash/reload followed by a run-end state loses no more than one flushed batch (~64 records / ~1.3 s) of telemetry; the rest is recoverable from the dev server.
- AC2: The server session file for a run contains its records exactly once (no duplication from partial + final uploads), and the automatic evaluation still runs once per run.
- AC3: Dev CLI tooling (`record-session`, `capture-gameplay`, `verify-dev-telemetry`) continues to work unchanged in behaviour.
- AC4: Full project test suite passes.

## Status

Open decision item — parked until the in-memory sink (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) lands. Do not implement concurrently with that item in the same worktree.

# Implement: seam-aware aimed fire

Implementation slice for seam-aware aimed fire (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC2). Every archetype routed through the shared aimed-shot method — Scout, `march` and the Raider — gains shortest-wrapped-path aiming in one place.

## Goal

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).
